title.zh: 卷四十九 列傳第九 孫處 蒯恩 劉鍾 虞丘進
title.en: Volume 49 Biographies 9: Sun Chu, Kuai En, Liu Zhong, Yu Qiujin
title.raw: 卷四十九 列傳第九 孫處 蒯恩 劉鍾 虞丘進 Volume 49 Biographies 9: Sun Chu, Kuai En, Liu Zhong, Yu Qiujin

sentences.zh: 列傳第九 孫處 蒯恩 劉鐘[1] 虞丘進

translations.literal: Biographies 9: Sun Chu, Kuai En, Liu Zhong, Yu Qiujin
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 9: Sun Chu, Kuai En, Liu Zhong, and Yu Qiujin

sentences.zh: 孫處，字季高，會稽永興人也。

translations.literal: Sun Chu, courtesy name Jigao, was a man of Yongxing in Kuaiji commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chu, whose courtesy name was Jigao, was a native of Yongxing in Kuaiji commandery.

sentences.zh: 籍注季高，故字行於世。

translations.literal: His household register recorded Jigao, so that courtesy name was used in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His name was entered in the register as Jigao, and that courtesy name is the one by which he was known.

sentences.zh: 少任氣。

translations.literal: In youth he was given to hot-tempered action.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was quick to take offense and act on impulse.

sentences.zh: 高祖東征孫恩，季高義樂隨。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor campaigned east against Sun En, Jigao gladly followed out of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor marched east against Sun En, Jigao gladly followed him out of loyalty.

sentences.zh: 高祖平定京邑，以為振武將軍，封新夷縣五等侯。

translations.literal: After the Founding Emperor pacified the capital region, he made him General Who Quells Martiality and enfeoffed him as a five-rank marquis of Xin'yi county.
translations.idiomatic: After the Founding Emperor secured the capital, he appointed Sun Chu General Who Quells Martiality and enfeoffed him as a fifth-rank marquis of Xin'yi county.

sentences.zh: 廣固之役，先登有功。

translations.literal: At the battle of Guanggu he was first to ascend and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: At the siege of Guanggu he was first over the wall and distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 盧循之難，於石頭捍柵，戍越城、查浦，破賊於新亭。

translations.literal: During the crisis of Lu Xun, he defended the palisade at Shitou, garrisoned Yuecheng and Zhapu, and defeated the rebels at Xinting.
translations.idiomatic: During Lu Xun's rebellion he held the palisade at Shitou, garrisoned Yuecheng and Zhapu, and routed the rebels at Xinting.

sentences.zh: 高祖謂季高曰：「此賊行破，應先傾其巢窟，令奔走之日，無所歸投，非卿莫能濟事。」

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor said to Jigao: "These rebels will soon be broken. We should first overturn their nest and stronghold, so that on the day they flee they will have nowhere to turn. No one but you can accomplish this."
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor told Jigao, "These rebels are on the verge of collapse. We must first destroy their base, so that when they flee they have nowhere to go. No one but you can see this through."

sentences.zh: 遣季高率眾三千，汎海襲番禺。

translations.literal: He dispatched Jigao to lead three thousand men across the sea to strike Panyu.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Jigao with three thousand men across the sea to strike Panyu.

sentences.zh: 初，賊不以海道為防，季高至東衝，去城十餘里，城內猶未知。

translations.literal: At first the rebels did not guard against the sea route. Jigao reached Dongchong, more than ten li from the city, and those inside still did not know.
translations.idiomatic: At first the rebels had not guarded the sea route. Jigao reached Dongchong, little more than ten li from the city, and those within still knew nothing of his approach.

sentences.zh: 循守戰士猶有數千人，城池甚固。

translations.literal: Xun's defending soldiers still numbered several thousand, and the city walls were very strong.
translations.idiomatic: Xun still had several thousand defenders, and the city was strongly fortified.

sentences.zh: 季高先焚舟艦，悉力登岸，會天大霧，四面陵城，即日克拔。

translations.literal: Jigao first burned his boats and ships, then exerted all his strength to go ashore. Heaven sent a great fog; from all four sides he scaled the city and took it the same day.
translations.idiomatic: Jigao burned his ships, landed with all his strength, and— as a heavy fog rolled in— assaulted the city from every side and took it that same day.

sentences.zh: 循父嘏、長史孫建之、司馬虞尪夫等，輕舟奔始興。

translations.literal: Xun's father Gu, Chief Clerk Sun Jianzhi, Major Yu Wangfu, and others fled in light boats to Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's father Gu, Chief Clerk Sun Jianzhi, Major Yu Wangfu, and others escaped in light boats to Shixing.

sentences.zh: 即分遣振武將軍沈田子等討平始興、南康、臨賀、始安嶺表諸郡。

translations.literal: He then dispatched General Who Quells Martiality Shen Tianzi and others to pacify Shixing, Nankang, Linhe, Shi'an, and the various commanderies south of the Ling mountains.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent General Who Quells Martiality Shen Tianzi and others to subdue Shixing, Nankang, Linhe, Shi'an, and the other commanderies beyond the Ling range.

sentences.zh: 循於左里奔走，而眾力猶盛，自嶺道還襲廣州。

translations.literal: Xun was in flight at Zuoli, but his forces were still strong; he returned by the Ling route to strike Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was in flight at Zuoli, but his army was still formidable, and he came back over the mountain passes to strike Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 季高距戰二十餘日，循乃破走，所殺萬餘人。

translations.literal: Jigao held him off in battle for more than twenty days; Xun was then broken and fled, and more than ten thousand were slain.
translations.idiomatic: Jigao fought him off for more than twenty days until Xun was routed and fled; more than ten thousand were killed.

sentences.zh: 追奔至鬱林，會病，不得窮討，循遂得走向交州。

translations.literal: Pursuing the fugitives to Yulin, he fell ill and could not pursue to the end, so Xun was able to flee toward Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued the fugitives as far as Yulin, but fell ill and could not finish the hunt, and Xun escaped toward Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 義熙七年四月，季高卒於晉康，時年五十三。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the seventh year of Yixi, Jigao died at Jinkang, aged fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the seventh year of Yixi, Jigao died at Jinkang at the age of fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 追贈龍驤將軍、南海太守，封侯官縣侯，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted General Who Leaps like a Dragon and Administrator of Nanhai, enfeoffed as Marquis of Houguan county with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made General Who Leaps like a Dragon and Administrator of Nanhai, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Houguan county with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 九年，高祖念季高之功，乃表曰：「孫季高嶺南之勳，已蒙褒贈。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, the Founding Emperor, mindful of Jigao's merit, submitted a memorial saying: "Sun Jigao's achievements south of the Ling have already received honorable posthumous grants.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, remembering Jigao's service, the Founding Emperor submitted a memorial: "Sun Jigao's exploits in the Lingnan region have already been honored with posthumous rewards.

sentences.zh: 臣更思惟盧循稔惡一紀，據有全域。

translations.literal: Your subject further reflects that Lu Xun accumulated wickedness for a full twelve-year cycle and held an entire region.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I further consider that Lu Xun had grown wicked over a full twelve-year cycle and held an entire region.

sentences.zh: 若令根本未拔，投奔有所，招合餘燼，猶能為虞；

translations.literal: If his root and trunk had not been uprooted and he had had somewhere to flee, gathering the embers of his force, he could still have caused trouble;
translations.idiomatic: Had his base not been destroyed and he still had somewhere to flee, he could have rallied the remnants of his force and remained a threat;

sentences.zh: 縣師遠討，方勤廟筭。

translations.literal: the imperial army would have had to campaign far away, and the court would have been busy with strategy in the temple.
translations.idiomatic: and the court would have had to dispatch armies on distant campaigns and labor over strategy in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 而季高汎海萬里，投命洪流，波激電邁，指日遄至，遂奄定南海，覆其巢窟，使循進退靡依，輕舟遠迸。

translations.literal: But Jigao crossed ten thousand li of sea, risking his life in the surging flood; waves leaped and lightning flashed as he arrived within days, then swiftly secured Nanhai and overturned their nest, leaving Xun with nowhere to advance or retreat and forcing him to flee in light boats.
translations.idiomatic: Instead Jigao crossed ten thousand li of open sea, staking his life on the raging waters; riding wind and wave he arrived within days, swiftly secured Nanhai, and destroyed their stronghold, leaving Xun with nowhere to turn and driving him to flee in light boats.

sentences.zh: 曾不旬月，妖凶殲殄。

translations.literal: In less than a full month, the demonic rebels were utterly destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: In less than a month the rebel scourge was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 蕩滌之功，實庸為大。

translations.literal: The merit of sweeping them away was truly great.
translations.idiomatic: The merit of clearing them away was truly great.

sentences.zh: 往年所贈，猶為未優。

translations.literal: What was granted in previous years was still insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: The rewards granted in earlier years were still inadequate.

sentences.zh: 愚謂宜更贈一州，即其本號，庶令忠勳不湮，勞臣增厲。」

translations.literal: I humbly propose that one further prefecture be granted posthumously, bearing his former title, so that loyal merit may not be lost and laboring ministers may be further encouraged."
translations.idiomatic: I humbly submit that one further prefecture should be granted posthumously under his former title, so that loyal service may not be forgotten and hardworking ministers may be further inspired."

sentences.zh: 重贈交州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the post of Inspector of Jiaozhou; his generalship remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Jigao was posthumously made Inspector of Jiaozhou, while his rank as general remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 子宗世卒，子欽公嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zongshi died; his grandson Qingong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zongshi died, and his grandson Qingong succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 欽公卒，子彥祖嗣。

translations.literal: Qingong died; his grandson Yanzu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Qingong died, his son Yanzu succeeded.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，國除。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi accepted the abdication, the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 蒯恩，字道恩，蘭陵承人也。

translations.literal: Kuai En, courtesy name Daoen, was a man of Cheng in Lanling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Kuai En, whose courtesy name was Daoen, was a native of Cheng in Lanling commandery.

sentences.zh: 高祖征孫恩，縣差為征民，充乙士，使伐馬芻。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor campaigned against Sun En, the county conscripted him as campaign labor, assigning him as a second-class soldier to cut horse fodder.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor marched against Sun En, the county drafted him for the campaign as a second-class soldier and set him to cutting horse fodder.

sentences.zh: 恩常負大束，兼倍餘人，每捨芻於地，歎曰：「大丈夫彎弓三石，柰何充馬士！」

translations.literal: En often carried large bundles, more than twice what others carried; each time he set fodder on the ground he sighed: "A great man who can draw a three-stone bow— why am I serving as horse fodder labor!"
translations.idiomatic: En often carried huge bundles— more than twice what the others could manage— and each time he dropped his load he would sigh, "A man who can draw a three-stone bow— and yet here I am cutting fodder like a stable hand!"

sentences.zh: 高祖聞之，即給器仗，恩大喜。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor heard this, he immediately gave him weapons and armor; En was greatly delighted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor heard this, he immediately gave En weapons and armor, and En was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 自征妖賊，常為先登，多斬首級。

translations.literal: From the campaigns against demonic rebels, he was often first to ascend and took many heads.
translations.idiomatic: From the campaigns against the rebels he was often first over the wall and took many enemy heads.

sentences.zh: 既習戰陣，膽力過人，誠心忠謹，未嘗有過失，甚見愛信。

translations.literal: Once practiced in battle formations, his courage and strength exceeded others'; he was sincerely loyal and careful, never committing a fault, and was greatly trusted and favored.
translations.idiomatic: Once seasoned in battle, his courage and strength surpassed those around him; he was sincerely loyal and careful, never once at fault, and won great trust and favor.

sentences.zh: 於婁縣戰，箭中左目。

translations.literal: In battle at Lou county, an arrow struck his left eye.
translations.idiomatic: In the fighting at Lou county an arrow struck his left eye.

sentences.zh: 從平京城，進定京邑，以寧遠將軍領幢。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying the capital and then securing the capital region, and was appointed General of Distant Pacification to command the standard-bearer guard.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the pacification of the capital and the securing of the capital region, and was made General of Distant Pacification with command of the standard-bearer guard.

sentences.zh: 隨振武將軍道規西討，虜桓仙客，克偃月壘，遂平江陵。

translations.literal: Following General Who Quells Martiality Daogui west on campaign, he captured Huan Xianke, took Yanyue fortress, and pacified Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: He followed General Who Quells Martiality Daogui on the western campaign, captured Huan Xianke, took Yanyue fortress, and pacified Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 義熙二年，賊張堅據應城反，恩擊破之，封都鄉侯。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yixi, the rebel Zhang Jian held Yingcheng and rebelled; En defeated him and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Duxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yixi the rebel Zhang Jian seized Yingcheng and rose in revolt; En defeated him and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Duxiang.

sentences.zh: 從伐廣固，又有戰功。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Guanggu and again had battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against Guanggu and again distinguished himself in battle.

sentences.zh: 盧循逼京邑，恩戰於查浦，賊退走。

translations.literal: When Lu Xun pressed the capital, En fought at Zhapu and the rebels retreated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Xun threatened the capital, En fought at Zhapu and drove the rebels back.

sentences.zh: 與王仲德等追破循別將范崇民於南陵。

translations.literal: With Wang Zhongde and others he pursued and defeated Lu Xun's deputy commander Fan Chongmin at Nanling.
translations.idiomatic: With Wang Zhongde and others he pursued and defeated Lu Xun's deputy commander Fan Chongmin at Nanling.

sentences.zh: 循既走還廣州，恩又領千餘人隨劉藩追徐道覆於始興，斬之。

translations.literal: After Xun had fled back to Guangzhou, En again led more than a thousand men following Liu Fan to pursue Xu Daofu at Shixing and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: After Xun fled back to Guangzhou, En led more than a thousand men under Liu Fan to pursue Xu Daofu at Shixing and killed him.

sentences.zh: 遷龍驤將軍、蘭陵太守。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General Who Leaps like a Dragon and Administrator of Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Leaps like a Dragon and made Administrator of Lanling.

sentences.zh: 高祖西征劉毅，恩與王鎮惡輕軍襲江陵，事在鎮惡傳。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor campaigned west against Liu Yi, En with Wang Zhen'e led light troops in a surprise attack on Jiangling; the account is in Zhen'e's biography.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor marched west against Liu Yi, En and Wang Zhen'e led light troops in a surprise attack on Jiangling— the full account appears in Zhen'e's biography.

sentences.zh: 以本官為太尉長兼行參軍，領眾二千，隨益州刺史朱齡石伐蜀。

translations.literal: Retaining his original office, he served as Clerk of the Grand Commandant with concurrent status as Acting Adjutant, leading two thousand troops following Inspector of Yizhou Zhu Lingshi to campaign against Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Retaining his original rank, he served as Clerk of the Grand Commandant with concurrent status as Acting Adjutant, leading two thousand men under Inspector of Yizhou Zhu Lingshi in the campaign against Shu.

sentences.zh: 至彭模，恩所領居前，大戰，自朝至日昃，勇氣益奮，賊破走。

translations.literal: At Pengmo, the force En commanded was in the van; in a great battle from morning until the sun slanted west, his courage grew fiercer and the rebels were broken and fled.
translations.idiomatic: At Pengmo his detachment led the van in a great battle that raged from morning until late afternoon; his courage only mounted, and the enemy was routed.

sentences.zh: 進平成都，擢為行參軍，改封北至縣五等男。

translations.literal: Advancing to pacify Chengdu, he was promoted to Acting Adjutant and re-enfeoffed as a five-rank baron of Beizhi county.
translations.idiomatic: After Chengdu was pacified he was promoted to Acting Adjutant and re-enfeoffed as a fifth-rank baron of Beizhi county.

sentences.zh: 高祖伐司馬休之及魯宗之，恩與建威將軍徐逵之前進。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor attacked Sima Xiuzhi and Lu Zongzhi, En advanced together with General Who Establishes Might Xu Dazhi.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor attacked Sima Xiuzhi and Lu Zongzhi, En advanced with General Who Establishes Might Xu Dazhi.

sentences.zh: 逵之敗沒，恩陳于堤下。

translations.literal: Dazhi was defeated and lost; En formed ranks below the dike.
translations.idiomatic: When Dazhi was defeated and killed, En drew up his ranks below the dike.

sentences.zh: 宗之子軌乘勝擊恩，矢下如雨，呼聲震地，恩整厲將士，置陣堅嚴。

translations.literal: Zongzhi's son Gui, seizing victory, attacked En; arrows fell like rain and shouts shook the earth. En rallied his officers and soldiers and set formations firm and strict.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhi's son Gui pressed his advantage and attacked En; arrows fell like rain and the battle cries shook the earth, but En rallied his men and held his formation firm.

sentences.zh: 軌屢衝之不動，知不可攻，乃退。

translations.literal: Gui charged repeatedly but could not move them; knowing he could not attack successfully, he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Gui charged again and again but could not break them; seeing that the attack would not succeed, he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 高祖善其能將軍持重。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor praised his ability to command the army with weight and steadiness.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor praised his ability to hold an army steady under pressure.

sentences.zh: 江陵平定，復追魯軌於石城。

translations.literal: After Jiangling was pacified, he again pursued Lu Gui at Shicheng.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiangling was pacified he again pursued Lu Gui at Shicheng.

sentences.zh: 軌棄城走，恩追至襄陽，宗之奔羌，恩與諸將追討，至魯陽關乃還。

translations.literal: Gui abandoned the city and fled; En pursued to Xiangyang. Zongzhi fled to the Qiang; En with the generals pursued and attacked to Luyang Pass and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Gui abandoned the city and fled; En pursued him to Xiangyang. Zongzhi fled to the Qiang, and En with the other generals pursued as far as Luyang Pass before turning back.

sentences.zh: 恩自從征討，每有危急，輒率先諸將，常陷堅破陣，不避艱嶮。

translations.literal: From the time En followed on campaigns, whenever there was danger he would take the lead among the generals, often breaking through hard positions and smashing formations, never shunning hardship and peril.
translations.idiomatic: From the time he first took the field, whenever danger arose En led the other generals, repeatedly breaking through strong positions and never shying from hardship or peril.

sentences.zh: 凡百餘戰，身被重創。

translations.literal: In more than a hundred battles altogether, he suffered grave wounds.
translations.idiomatic: In more than a hundred battles he suffered grave wounds.

sentences.zh: 高祖錄其前後功勞，封新寧縣男，食邑五百戶。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor recorded his merits before and after and enfeoffed him as Baron of Xining county with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor recorded his accumulated service and enfeoffed him as Baron of Xining county with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 高祖世子為征虜將軍，恩以大府佐領中兵參軍，隨府轉中兵參軍。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor's heir was General Who Pacifies Barbarians, En as grand headquarters aide served as Central Army Adjutant; when the headquarters transferred he became Central Army Adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor's heir was made General Who Pacifies Barbarians, En served as Central Army Adjutant on the grand headquarters staff, and when the headquarters moved he retained that post.

sentences.zh: 高祖北伐，留恩侍衛世子，命朝士與之交。

translations.literal: On the Founding Emperor's northern campaign, En was left to guard the heir; he was ordered to associate with court gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: On the Founding Emperor's northern campaign En was left to guard the heir, and was instructed to keep company with court gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 恩益自謙損，與人語常呼官位，而自稱為鄙人。

translations.literal: En became ever more humble; when speaking with others he always addressed them by their official titles and called himself "this lowly man."
translations.idiomatic: En grew ever more modest; in conversation he always addressed others by their official titles and called himself "this humble man."

sentences.zh: 撫待士卒，甚有紀綱，眾咸親附之。

translations.literal: In managing soldiers he had strict discipline, and all drew close and attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: He treated his soldiers with firm discipline, and they all drew close to him.

sentences.zh: 遷諮議參軍，轉輔國將軍、淮陵太守。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Advisory Adjutant, then transferred to General Who Assists the State and Administrator of Huailing.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Advisory Adjutant, then transferred to General Who Assists the State and made Administrator of Huailing.

sentences.zh: 世子開府，又為從事中郎，轉司馬，將軍、太守如故。

translations.literal: When the heir opened a headquarters, he again served as Attendant Secretary, then transferred to Major; his generalship and prefecture remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir opened his own headquarters En served as Attendant Secretary, then as Major, while retaining his rank as general and his prefecture.

sentences.zh: 入關迎桂陽公義真。

translations.literal: He entered the passes to meet the Duke of Guiyang, Yizhen.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the passes to meet the Duke of Guiyang, Yizhen.

sentences.zh: 義真還至青泥，為佛佛虜所追，恩斷後，力戰連日。

translations.literal: When Yizhen returned to Qingni, he was pursued by the Babao barbarians; En covered the rear and fought fiercely for days.
translations.idiomatic: When Yizhen reached Qingni on his return, the Babao barbarians pursued him; En covered the rear and fought fiercely for days on end.

sentences.zh: 義真前軍奔散，恩軍人亦盡，為虜所執，死於虜中。

translations.literal: Yizhen's vanguard scattered and fled; En's soldiers were also exhausted; he was captured by the barbarians and died among them.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen's vanguard broke and fled; En's men were also spent, and he was captured by the enemy and died in captivity.

sentences.zh: 子國才嗣。

translations.literal: His son Guocai succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guocai succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 國才卒，子慧度嗣。

translations.literal: Guocai died; his son Huidu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Guocai died, his son Huidu succeeded.

sentences.zh: 慧度卒，無子，國除。

translations.literal: Huidu died without a son; the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Huidu died without an heir, the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 劉鍾，字世之，彭城彭城人也。

translations.literal: Liu Zhong, courtesy name Shizhi, was a man of Pengcheng in Pengcheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhong, whose courtesy name was Shizhi, was a native of Pengcheng in Pengcheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 少孤，依鄉人中山太守劉回共居。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he lived together with his fellow townsman Liu Hui, Administrator of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he lived with his fellow townsman Liu Hui, Administrator of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 幼有志力，常慷慨於貧賤。

translations.literal: As a child he had resolution and strength, and often felt passionate indignation in poverty and low station.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he had strength of will, and often burned with ambition despite his poverty and low station.

sentences.zh: 隆安四年，高祖伐孫恩，鍾願從餘姚、浹口攻句章、海鹽、婁縣，皆摧堅陷陣，每有戰功。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Long'an, the Founding Emperor attacked Sun En; Zhong volunteered to follow, attacking Juzhang, Haiyan, and Lou county from Yuyao and Jiakou—all smashing hard positions and breaking formations, with merit in every battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Long'an the Founding Emperor marched against Sun En; Zhong volunteered and fought at Juzhang, Haiyan, and Lou county from Yuyao and Jiakou, breaking through every strong position and winning merit in every engagement.

sentences.zh: 為劉牢之鎮北參軍督護。

translations.literal: He served as Inspector-and-Protector under Liu Lao's Northern Pacification Army Adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Inspector-and-Protector on the staff of Liu Lao, Northern Pacification Army Adjutant.

sentences.zh: 高祖每有戎事，鍾不辭艱劇，專心盡力，甚見愛信。

translations.literal: Whenever the Founding Emperor had military affairs, Zhong never declined hardship and toil, devoting heart and strength; he was greatly trusted and favored.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Founding Emperor took the field, Zhong never shrank from hardship, giving himself wholly to the task, and won great trust and favor.

sentences.zh: 義旗將建，高祖版鍾為郡主簿。

translations.literal: As the righteous banner was about to be raised, the Founding Emperor issued Zhong a commission as chief clerk of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: As the righteous banner was about to be raised, the Founding Emperor commissioned Zhong chief clerk of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 明日，從入京城。

translations.literal: The next day he followed into the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he entered the capital with the army.

sentences.zh: 將向京邑，高祖命曰：「預是彭、沛鄉人赴義者，並可依劉主簿。」

translations.literal: When about to march on the capital region, the Founding Emperor ordered: "All who from Peng and Pei country have come out in righteousness may attach themselves to Chief Clerk Liu."
translations.idiomatic: As they prepared to march on the capital, the Founding Emperor ordered, "All men of Peng and Pei who have risen in the cause may report to Chief Clerk Liu."

sentences.zh: 於是立為義隊，恆在左右，連戰皆捷。

translations.literal: Thereupon a righteous-force unit was formed with Zhong always at his side; battle after battle was victorious.
translations.idiomatic: A volunteer unit was formed with Zhong always at the Founding Emperor's side, and battle after battle was won.

sentences.zh: 明日，桓謙屯於東陵，卞範之屯覆舟山西，高祖疑賊有伏兵，顧視左右，正見鍾，謂之曰：「此山下當有伏兵，卿可率部下稍往撲之。」

translations.literal: The next day Huan Qian encamped at Dongling and Bian Fanzhi at west of Fuzhou mountain. The Founding Emperor suspected the enemy had hidden troops; looking left and right, he saw Zhong and said to him: "There ought to be hidden troops below this mountain. You may lead your subordinates a little ways forward to flush them out."
translations.idiomatic: The next day Huan Qian encamped at Dongling and Bian Fanzhi west of Fuzhou mountain. Suspecting an ambush, the Founding Emperor looked about and spotted Zhong. "There are likely hidden troops on this hillside," he said. "Take your men forward and flush them out."

sentences.zh: 鍾應聲馳進，果有伏兵數百，一時奔走。

translations.literal: Zhong at once galloped forward; indeed there were several hundred hidden troops who all fled at once.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong galloped forward at once; sure enough, several hundred hidden troops broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 桓玄西奔，其夕，高祖止桓謙故營，遣鍾宿據東府，轉鎮軍參軍督護。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan fled west; that evening the Founding Emperor halted at Huan Qian's former camp and sent Zhong to garrison the Eastern Palace; he was transferred to Inspector-and-Protector under the Army Pacification General.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan fled west; that evening the Founding Emperor camped at Huan Qian's former position and sent Zhong to hold the Eastern Palace. Zhong was then made Inspector-and-Protector on the Army Pacification General's staff.

sentences.zh: 桓歆寇歷陽，遣鍾助豫州刺史魏詠之討之，歆即奔迸。

translations.literal: Huan Xin raided Liyang; he sent Zhong to assist Inspector of Yuzhou Wei Yongzhi to attack him; Xin at once fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xin raided Liyang, the Founding Emperor sent Zhong to assist Inspector of Yuzhou Wei Yongzhi; Xin fled at once.

sentences.zh: 除南齊國內史，封安丘縣五等侯。

translations.literal: He was appointed Interior Minister of Nanqi kingdom and enfeoffed as a five-rank marquis of Anqiu county.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Interior Minister of the principality of Nanqi and enfeoffed as a fifth-rank marquis of Anqiu county.

sentences.zh: 自陳情事，改葬父祖及親屬十喪，高祖厚加資給。

translations.literal: He stated his personal circumstances: reburial of his father, grandfather, and ten relatives' funerals; the Founding Emperor generously provided funds.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to reinter his father, grandfather, and ten other relatives; the Founding Emperor generously provided the funds.

sentences.zh: 轉車騎長史，兼行參軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief Clerk of Chariots and Cavalry with concurrent status as Acting Adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Chief Clerk of Chariots and Cavalry with concurrent status as Acting Adjutant.

sentences.zh: 司馬叔璠與彭城劉謐、劉懷玉等自蕃城攻鄒山，魯郡太守徐邕失守，鍾率軍討平之。

translations.literal: Sima Shufan with Liu Mi and Liu Huaiyu of Pengcheng and others attacked Zou mountain from Fancheng; Administrator of Lu commandery Xu Yong lost the city; Zhong led troops to attack and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shufan with Liu Mi, Liu Huaiyu of Pengcheng, and others attacked Zou mountain from Fancheng; when Administrator of Lu Xu Yong lost the city, Zhong led troops to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 從征廣固。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Guanggu.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against Guanggu.

sentences.zh: 孟龍符陷沒，鍾率左右直入，取其尸而反。

translations.literal: Meng Longfu was killed in action; Zhong led his personal guard straight in, recovered the corpse and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Meng Longfu was killed in action, Zhong led his personal guard straight into the enemy lines, recovered the body, and returned.

sentences.zh: 除振武將軍、中兵參軍，代龍符領廣川太守。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Quells Martiality and Central Army Adjutant, succeeding Longfu as Administrator of Guangchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General Who Quells Martiality and Central Army Adjutant, succeeding Longfu as Administrator of Guangchuan.

sentences.zh: 盧循逼京邑，徐赤軍違處分，敗於南岸。

translations.literal: When Lu Xun pressed the capital, Xu Chi's army disobeyed orders and was defeated on the south bank.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Xun threatened the capital, Xu Chi's army disobeyed orders and was defeated on the south bank.

sentences.zh: 鍾率麾下距柵，身被重創，賊不得入。

translations.literal: Zhong led his subordinates to hold the palisade; though he suffered grave wounds, the rebels could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong led his men to hold the palisade; though he suffered grave wounds, the rebels could not break through.

sentences.zh: 循南走，鍾與輔國將軍王仲德追之。

translations.literal: Xun fled south; Zhong with General Who Assists the State Wang Zhongde pursued.
translations.idiomatic: Xun fled south, and Zhong with General Who Assists the State Wang Zhongde pursued him.

sentences.zh: 循先留別帥范崇民以精兵高艦據南陵，夾屯兩岸。

translations.literal: Xun had earlier left deputy commander Fan Chongmin with elite troops and tall warships to hold Nanling, encamped on both banks.
translations.idiomatic: Xun had earlier left his deputy Fan Chongmin with elite troops and tall warships to hold Nanling, with camps on both banks of the river.

sentences.zh: 鍾自行覘賊，天霧，賊鉤得其舸；

translations.literal: Zhong personally went to reconnoiter the enemy; fog shrouded the sky, and the enemy hooked and seized his boat;
translations.idiomatic: Zhong went personally to scout the enemy; fog rolled in, and the rebels hooked and seized his boat;

sentences.zh: 鍾因率左右攻艦戶，賊遽閉戶距之，鍾乃徐還。

translations.literal: Zhong thereupon led his personal guard to attack the ship's hatch; the rebels hastily closed the hatch to hold him off, and Zhong then withdrew slowly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong led his personal guard to attack the hatch of the enemy ship, but the rebels slammed it shut; Zhong then withdrew at an unhurried pace.

sentences.zh: 與仲德攻崇民，崇民敗走。

translations.literal: With Zhongde he attacked Chongmin; Chongmin was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He and Zhongde attacked Chongmin, who was routed and fled.

sentences.zh: 鍾追討百里，燒其船乘。

translations.literal: Zhong pursued for a hundred li and burned their boats and transport.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong pursued them for a hundred li and burned their ships.

sentences.zh: 又隨劉藩追徐道覆於始興，斬之。

translations.literal: He again followed Liu Fan to pursue Xu Daofu at Shixing and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Liu Fan to pursue Xu Daofu at Shixing and killed him.

sentences.zh: 補太尉行參軍、寧朔將軍、下邳太守。

translations.literal: He was appointed Acting Adjutant of the Grand Commandant, General of Pacifying the North, and Administrator of Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Acting Adjutant on the Grand Commandant's staff, General of Pacifying the North, and Administrator of Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 代孟懷玉領石頭戍事。

translations.literal: He succeeded Meng Huaiyu in charge of the garrison at Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded Meng Huaiyu as commander of the Shitou garrison.

sentences.zh: 高祖討劉毅，鍾率軍繼王鎮惡。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor attacked Liu Yi, Zhong led troops following Wang Zhen'e.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor marched against Liu Yi, Zhong led an army in support of Wang Zhen'e.

sentences.zh: 江陵平定，仍隨朱齡石伐蜀，為前鋒，由外水至于彭模，去成都二百里。

translations.literal: After Jiangling was pacified, he again followed Zhu Lingshi to campaign against Shu as vanguard, going by the outer water route to Pengmo, two hundred li from Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiangling was pacified he again followed Zhu Lingshi against Shu as vanguard, taking the outer water route to Pengmo, two hundred li from Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 偽冠軍征討督護譙亢等兩岸連營，曾樓重柵，眾號三萬。

translations.literal: The false regime's Champion General and Campaign Protector Qiao Kang and others had linked camps on both banks, with layered towers and heavy palisades, their force proclaimed at thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy Champion General and Campaign Protector Qiao Kang and others had linked camps on both banks with layered towers and heavy palisades; their force was said to number thirty thousand.

sentences.zh: 鍾于時腳疾不能行，齡石乃詣鍾謀曰：「今天時盛熱，而賊嚴兵固險，攻之未必可拔，祗增疲困。

translations.literal: Zhong at the time had a foot ailment and could not walk; Lingshi then went to Zhong to consult, saying: "Today the season is fiercely hot, and the enemy holds troops firm in strong positions; an attack may not necessarily succeed and will only increase exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was then afflicted with a foot ailment and could not walk; Lingshi came to consult him. "The weather is fiercely hot," he said, "and the enemy holds strong positions with a tight defense. An assault may not succeed and will only wear our men down.

sentences.zh: 計其人情恇撓，必不久安，且欲養銳息兵，以伺其隙；

translations.literal: I calculate that their men's spirits are timid and unsettled and will not long remain steady; moreover we should nurture sharpness and rest the army to watch for an opening;
translations.idiomatic: I reckon their troops are timid and restless and will not hold firm for long. We should conserve our strength, rest the army, and wait for an opening;

sentences.zh: 隙而乘之，乃可捷事。

translations.literal: when an opening appears, seize it, and then the affair can be swiftly concluded.
translations.idiomatic: and when the moment comes, strike— that is how we can win quickly.

sentences.zh: 然決機兩陳，公本有所委，卿意謂何？」

translations.literal: Yet two plans for decision are set forth; the lord originally had someone entrusted— what does your view say?"
translations.idiomatic: Two plans are before us, and the lord originally entrusted this decision to you— what is your view?"

sentences.zh: 鍾曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Zhong said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong replied, "I disagree.

sentences.zh: 前揚聲言大眾向內水，譙道福不敢舍涪城。

translations.literal: Earlier we proclaimed that the main force was heading by the inner water route, so Qiao Daofu did not dare leave Fucheng.
translations.idiomatic: We had spread word that the main army was advancing by the inner water route, so Qiao Daofu did not dare leave Fucheng.

sentences.zh: 今重軍卒至，出其不意，蜀人已破膽矣。

translations.literal: Now our heavy army has suddenly arrived, catching them unawares; the men of Shu are already broken in courage.
translations.idiomatic: Now our main force has arrived unexpectedly, and the Shu troops have already lost their nerve.

sentences.zh: 賊今阻兵守險，是其懼不敢戰，非能持久堅守也。

translations.literal: The rebels now block with troops and hold strong positions because they fear and dare not fight; it is not that they can long hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy holds the passes because they are afraid to fight, not because they can sustain a long defense.

sentences.zh: 因其凶懼，盡銳攻之，其勢必克。

translations.literal: Taking advantage of their terror and fear, attack with all sharpness; the momentum will surely overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Strike now, while they are still terrified, with every available man— we are sure to break them.

sentences.zh: 鼓行而進，成都必不能守矣。

translations.literal: Advancing with drums beating, Chengdu will surely be unable to hold.
translations.idiomatic: March in with drums beating, and Chengdu will not be able to hold.

sentences.zh: 今若緩兵相守，彼將知人虛實，涪軍忽并來力距我，人情既安，良將又集，此求戰不獲，軍食無資，當為蜀子虜耳。」

translations.literal: If we now slow the army and stand in stalemate, they will learn our true strength and weakness; the Fucheng army may suddenly join and forcefully resist us. Once their men's spirits are settled and good generals gather, we will seek battle in vain and have no supplies for the army—we will become captives of the Shu people."
translations.idiomatic: If we hold back now, they will learn our true strength; the Fucheng army may suddenly unite against us. Once their troops regain confidence and their best commanders assemble, we will fail to bring them to battle and run out of provisions— and become prisoners of Shu."

sentences.zh: 齡石從之。

translations.literal: Lingshi followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Lingshi accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 明日進攻，陷其二城，斬其大將侯輝、譙詵，逕平成都。

translations.literal: The next day they advanced in attack, took two cities, beheaded the enemy generals Hou Hui and Qiao Shen, and straightway pacified Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they attacked, took two cities, killed the enemy generals Hou Hui and Qiao Shen, and went on to pacify Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 以廣固功，封永新縣男，食邑五百戶。

translations.literal: For merit at Guanggu he was enfeoffed as Baron of Yongxin county with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his service at Guanggu he was enfeoffed as Baron of Yongxin county with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中、太尉參軍事、龍驤將軍、高陽內史，領石頭戍事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attendant Within the Yellow Gates, Army Staff Officer of the Grand Commandant, General Who Leaps like a Dragon, and Interior Minister of Gaoyang, in charge of the garrison at Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant Within the Yellow Gates, Army Staff Officer on the Grand Commandant's staff, General Who Leaps like a Dragon, and Interior Minister of Gaoyang, while retaining command of the Shitou garrison.

sentences.zh: 高祖討司馬休之，前軍將軍道憐留鎮東府，領屯兵。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor attacked Sima Xiuzhi, Vanguard Army General Daolian remained to guard the Eastern Palace and command the garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor marched against Sima Xiuzhi, Vanguard Army General Daolian remained to guard the Eastern Palace and command the garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 冶亭羣盜數百夜襲鍾壘，距擊破之。

translations.literal: Several hundred bandits at Yeting raided Zhong's camp by night; he held them off and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred bandits at Yeting raided Zhong's camp by night; he fought them off and routed them.

sentences.zh: 時大軍外討，京邑擾懼，鍾以不能鎮遏，降號建威將軍。

translations.literal: At the time the main army was campaigning abroad and the capital was thrown into alarm and fear; because Zhong could not keep order, his title was reduced to General Who Establishes Might.
translations.idiomatic: While the main army was away on campaign the capital was thrown into alarm; because Zhong could not restore order, his title was reduced to General Who Establishes Might.

sentences.zh: 平蜀功，應封四百戶男，以先有封爵，減戶以賜次子敬順高昌縣男，食邑百戶。

translations.literal: For his merit in pacifying Shu he should have been enfeoffed as a baron with a fief of four hundred households; because he already held a title, households were reduced and his second son Jingshun was granted Baron of Gaochang county with a fief of one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his service in pacifying Shu he was due a barony of four hundred households; because he already held a title, the grant was reduced and his second son Jingshun was made Baron of Gaochang county with a fief of one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋復本號龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: Soon his former title of General Who Leaps like a Dragon was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his former rank of General Who Leaps like a Dragon was restored.

sentences.zh: 十二年，高祖北伐，復留鎮居守，增其兵力，又命府置佐史。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, on the Founding Emperor's northern campaign, Zhong was again left to guard the capital; his military strength was increased, and he was ordered to appoint staff assistants and clerks for his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, when the Founding Emperor marched north, Zhong was again left to guard the capital; his forces were increased, and he was ordered to appoint staff assistants and clerks for his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史道憐獻名馬三匹，并精麗乘具，高祖悉以賜鍾三子。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jingzhou Daolian presented three famous horses together with fine harness and riding gear; the Founding Emperor gave them all to Zhong's three sons.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector of Jingzhou Daolian presented three famous horses with fine harness and riding gear, and the Founding Emperor gave them all to Zhong's three sons.

sentences.zh: 十四年，遷右衞將軍，龍驤將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to Right Guards General, while his rank as General Who Leaps like a Dragon remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was made Right Guards General, while retaining his rank as General Who Leaps like a Dragon.

sentences.zh: 元熙元年卒，時年四十三。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanxi he died, aged forty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanxi he died at the age of forty-three.

sentences.zh: 子敬義嗣。

translations.literal: His son Jingyi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingyi succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 敬義官至馬頭太守，卒。

translations.literal: Jingyi reached the office of Administrator of Matou and died.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyi rose to Administrator of Matou and died in office.

sentences.zh: 子國重嗣，齊受禪，國除。

translations.literal: His son Guozhong succeeded; when Qi received the abdication, the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guozhong succeeded; when Qi accepted the abdication, the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 鍾次子高昌男敬順，卒，子國須嗣。

translations.literal: Zhong's second son Jingshun, Baron of Gaochang, died; his son Guoxu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong's second son Jingshun, Baron of Gaochang, died, and his son Guoxu succeeded.

sentences.zh: 須卒，無子，國除。

translations.literal: Xu died without a son; the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu died without an heir, the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 虞丘進字豫之，東海郯人也。

translations.literal: Yu Qiujin, courtesy name Yuzhi, was a man of Tan in Donghai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qiujin, whose courtesy name was Yuzhi, was a native of Tan in Donghai commandery.

sentences.zh: 少時隨謝玄討苻堅，有功，封關內侯。

translations.literal: In youth he followed Xie Xuan in the campaign against Fu Jian and had merit; he was enfeoffed as Marquis Within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he followed Xie Xuan against Fu Jian and distinguished himself; he was enfeoffed as Marquis Within the Passes.

sentences.zh: 隆安中，從高祖征孫恩，戍句章城，被圍數十日，無日不戰，身被數創。

translations.literal: During Long'an he followed the Founding Emperor against Sun En, garrisoned Juzhang city, was besieged for several tens of days, fought every day without exception, and suffered several wounds.
translations.idiomatic: During Long'an he followed the Founding Emperor against Sun En, garrisoned Juzhang, and was besieged for several tens of days; he fought every day and suffered several wounds.

sentences.zh: 至餘姚呵浦，破賊張驃，追至海鹽故治及婁縣。

translations.literal: At Yuyao Hapu he defeated the rebel Zhang Biao and pursued to the former seat of Haiyan and Lou county.
translations.idiomatic: At Yuyao Hapu he defeated the rebel Zhang Biao and pursued as far as the former seat of Haiyan and Lou county.

sentences.zh: 於蒲濤口與孫恩水戰，又被重創。

translations.literal: At Putao Ford he fought Sun En on the water and again suffered grave wounds.
translations.idiomatic: At Putao Ford he fought Sun En on the water and again suffered grave wounds.

sentences.zh: 追恩至鬱洲，又至石鹿頭，還海鹽大柱，頻戰有功。

translations.literal: Pursuing En to Yuzhou and then to Shilutou, he returned to Haiyan Dazhu and repeatedly fought with merit.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued En to Yuzhou and then to Shilutou, returned to Haiyan Dazhu, and won merit in repeated engagements.

sentences.zh: 元興元年，又從高祖東征臨海，於石步固與盧循相守二十餘日。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanxing he again followed the Founding Emperor east against Linhai and at Shibu fortress faced Lu Xun for more than twenty days.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanxing he again followed the Founding Emperor east against Linhai and at Shibu fortress held Lu Xun at bay for more than twenty days.

sentences.zh: 二年，又從高祖至東陽，破徐道覆。

translations.literal: In the second year he again followed the Founding Emperor to Dongyang and defeated Xu Daofu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he again followed the Founding Emperor to Dongyang and defeated Xu Daofu.

sentences.zh: 其年，又至臨松穴破賊，追至永嘉千江，又至安固，累戰皆有功。

translations.literal: That year he again went to Linsong Pass, defeated the rebels, pursued to Yongjia Qianjiang and then to Angu, and in repeated battles all had merit.
translations.idiomatic: That year he again went to Linsong Pass, defeated the rebels, pursued to Yongjia Qianjiang and then to Angu, and distinguished himself in battle after battle.

sentences.zh: 三年，從平京城，定京邑，除燕國內史。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed in pacifying the capital and securing the capital region, and was appointed Interior Minister of Yan principality.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he followed the pacification of the capital and the securing of the capital region, and was made Interior Minister of the principality of Yan.

sentences.zh: 義熙二年，除龍驤將軍，封龍川縣五等侯。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yixi he was appointed General Who Leaps like a Dragon and enfeoffed as a five-rank marquis of Longchuan county.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yixi he was made General Who Leaps like a Dragon and enfeoffed as a fifth-rank marquis of Longchuan county.

sentences.zh: 從高祖伐廣固，於臨朐破賊。

translations.literal: He followed the Founding Emperor in the campaign against Guanggu and defeated the rebels at Linqu.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Founding Emperor's campaign against Guanggu and routed the enemy at Linqu.

sentences.zh: 盧循逼京邑，孟昶、諸葛長民等建議奉天子過江，進廷議不可，面折昶等，高祖甚嘉之。

translations.literal: When Lu Xun pressed the capital, Meng Chang, Zhuge Changmin, and others proposed escorting the Son of Heaven across the river; Jin argued in court that this was unacceptable and rebutted Chang and the others to their faces. The Founding Emperor greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Xun threatened the capital, Meng Chang, Zhuge Changmin, and others proposed moving the emperor south across the Yangzi. Jin argued before the court that this was unacceptable and openly refuted Chang and his allies; the Founding Emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 獻計伐樹，樹柵石頭。

translations.literal: He offered a plan to cut trees and build a palisade at Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed felling trees to build a palisade at Shitou.

sentences.zh: 除鄱陽太守，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He was appointed Administrator of Poyang; his generalship remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Administrator of Poyang while retaining his rank as general.

sentences.zh: 統馬步十八隊，於東道出鄱陽，至五畝嶠。

translations.literal: He commanded eighteen cavalry and infantry units, marching east from Poyang to Wumu Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded eighteen cavalry and infantry detachments, advancing east from Poyang to Wumu Pass.

sentences.zh: 循遣將英紏為上饒令。

translations.literal: Xun dispatched the general Ying Gou to serve as magistrate of Shangrao.
translations.idiomatic: Xun sent the general Ying Gou to serve as magistrate of Shangrao.

sentences.zh: 千餘人守故城，進攻破之。

translations.literal: More than a thousand men held the old city; Jin advanced, attacked, and took it.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand men held the old city; Jin advanced, attacked, and captured it.

sentences.zh: 循又遣童敏之為鄱陽太守，據郡，進從餘干步道趣鄱陽，敏之退走，追破之，斬首數百。

translations.literal: Xun again dispatched Tong Minzhi as Administrator of Poyang to hold the commandery; Jin advanced by the land route from Yugan toward Poyang; Minzhi retreated and fled; Jin pursued, defeated him, and took several hundred heads.
translations.idiomatic: Xun then sent Tong Minzhi as Administrator of Poyang to hold the commandery. Jin advanced overland from Yugan toward Poyang; Minzhi fled, and Jin pursued, defeated him, and took several hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 復隨劉藩至始興，討斬徐道覆。

translations.literal: He again followed Liu Fan to Shixing and attacked and beheaded Xu Daofu.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Liu Fan to Shixing, where Xu Daofu was hunted down and killed.

sentences.zh: 八年，除寧蠻護軍、尋陽太守，領文武二年從征劉毅。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed Protector of the Ningman and Administrator of Xunyang, holding civil and military authority; two years later he followed the campaign against Liu Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was made Protector of the Ningman and Administrator of Xunyang, with civil and military authority. He then followed the campaign against Liu Yi.

sentences.zh: 事平，補太尉行參軍，尋加振威將軍。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, he was appointed Acting Adjutant of the Grand Commandant and soon promoted to General Who Quells Martiality.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign he was appointed Acting Adjutant on the Grand Commandant's staff and soon promoted to General Who Quells Martiality.

sentences.zh: 九年，以前後功封望蔡縣男，食邑五百戶，加龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, for his accumulated merits he was enfeoffed as Baron of Wangcai county with a fief of five hundred households and promoted to General Who Leaps like a Dragon.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, for his accumulated service he was enfeoffed as Baron of Wangcai county with a fief of five hundred households and made General Who Leaps like a Dragon.

sentences.zh: 討司馬休之，又有戰功。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Sima Xiuzhi he again had battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Sima Xiuzhi he again distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 軍還，除輔國將軍、山陽太守。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was appointed General Who Assists the State and Administrator of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned he was made General Who Assists the State and Administrator of Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 宋臺令書除秦郡太守，督陳留郡事，將軍如故。

translations.literal: An order from the Song administration appointed him Administrator of Qin commandery with supervision over Chenliu commandery; his generalship remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: An order from the Song administration appointed him Administrator of Qin commandery with supervisory authority over Chenliu, while his rank as general remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 元熙二年，宋王令書以為高祖第四子義康右將軍司馬。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanxi, an order from the Prince of Song appointed him Major on the staff of the Right General for the Founding Emperor's fourth son Yikang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanxi an order from the Prince of Song appointed him Major on the staff of Right General Yikang, the Founding Emperor's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 永初二年，遷太子右衛率。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongchu he was transferred to Right Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongchu he was made Right Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.

sentences.zh: 明年，卒官。

translations.literal: The next year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he died in office.

sentences.zh: 時年六十。

translations.literal: He was then sixty years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was sixty years old.

sentences.zh: 追論討司馬休之功，進爵為子，增邑三百戶。

translations.literal: His merit in the campaign against Sima Xiuzhi was reviewed posthumously; his rank was advanced to viscount and his fief increased by three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: His service against Sima Xiuzhi was reviewed posthumously; his rank was raised to viscount and his fief increased by three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 子耕嗣。

translations.literal: His son Geng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Geng succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 耕卒，子襲祖嗣。

translations.literal: Geng died; his son Xizu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Geng died, his son Xizu succeeded.

sentences.zh: 襲祖卒，世寶嗣。

translations.literal: Xizu died; Shibao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Xizu died, Shibao succeeded.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，國除。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi accepted the abdication, the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：《詩》云：「無言不酬，無德不報。」

translations.literal: The historiographer says: The Odes say: "No word goes unrewarded, no virtue goes unrequited."
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: The Odes say, "No word goes unrewarded, no virtue goes unrequited."

sentences.zh: 此諸將並起自豎夫，出於皁隸蒭牧之下，徒以心一乎主，故能奮其鱗翼。

translations.literal: These generals all rose from common laborers, emerging from beneath menials who cut fodder and tended herds; solely because their hearts were single toward their lord, they were able to spread their scales and wings.
translations.idiomatic: These generals all rose from common laborers— men who had come up from the ranks of grooms and fodder-cutters— and only because their loyalty to their lord was undivided were they able to spread their wings and soar.

sentences.zh: 至於推鋒轉戰，百死而不顧一生，蓋由其心一也。

translations.literal: As for pressing the vanguard and turning in battle, facing a hundred deaths without sparing one life— this was because their hearts were single.
translations.idiomatic: When it came to leading charges and fighting battle after battle, risking death a hundred times without thought for their own lives— that too sprang from undivided loyalty.

sentences.zh: 遂饗封侯之報，詩人之言，信矣！

translations.literal: Thus they enjoyed the reward of enfeoffment as marquises; the poet's words are true indeed!
translations.idiomatic: And so they received the reward of marquisates— the poet spoke truly indeed!
